meow.summary: Selection-first modal editing, the grammar every key here builds on.
meow.example: =w= marks a word, then =d= deletes it; you see the target before you act.

undo-tree.summary: Undo history drawn as a tree, so an undone change is never lost.
undo-tree.example: =SPC b u= shows the history, and the arrow keys walk through it.

structural-editing.summary: Keeps brackets balanced as you edit, and re-indents Lisp as you type.
structural-editing.example: Deleting never breaks a pair, and =C-)= pulls the next expression inside.

surround.summary: Adds, changes and removes the pair around a selection.
surround.example: =SPC c s= wraps the selection in quotes or brackets.

syntax-things.summary: Meow selects by syntax: functions, classes and parameters.
syntax-things.example: =, f= selects inside the current function in a Tree-sitter buffer.

visual-replace.summary: Regexp replacement that shows each match and its result as you type.
visual-replace.example: =SPC s r= previews the replacement before you commit to it.

whitespace-cleanup.summary: Removes trailing whitespace from the lines you changed, and no others.
whitespace-cleanup.example: Saving leaves untouched lines out of the diff; =SPC c w= cleans a whole buffer.

snippets.summary: Expands short templates that you keep in your own folder.
snippets.example: =SPC i s= picks a snippet for this kind of file.

spelling.summary: Corrects spelling through the completion list.
spelling.example: =SPC s p= lists the errors in this buffer.

completion.summary: Filterable lists for every prompt, and completion as you type.
completion.example: =SPC b b= switches buffer, and =SPC s d= searches a project.

directory-switch.summary: Offers recent and project directories at any file prompt.
directory-switch.example: =SPC f D= goes to a directory you used before.

jump.summary: Jumps anywhere on screen by typing a character and a letter.
jump.example: =SPC j j= puts letters on each match, then you press one.

window-picker.summary: Picks a window by letter when a frame holds several.
window-picker.example: =SPC w w= labels each window, and a letter jumps there.

workspaces.summary: One tab per project, each listing only its own buffers.
workspaces.example: =SPC p p= opens a project in a workspace of its own.

file-tree.summary: A project tree in a sidebar that follows the file you are in.
file-tree.example: =SPC t d= opens the tree, and =SPC f t= finds this file in it.

dired-extras.summary: Colours, filtering and copy-and-paste in the file manager.
dired-extras.example: =SPC d= opens the directory, with file types in colour.

doom-look.summary: The Sonokai theme and an informative mode line, instead of the built-in look.
doom-look.example: =SPC t t= flips between dark and light themes.

icons.summary: File and symbol icons in lists and in the file manager.
icons.example: =SPC f f= shows an icon beside each file; it needs a Nerd Font.

code-display.summary: Colours brackets by depth and draws a guide at each indentation level.
code-display.example: Matching brackets share a colour in code.

ui-polish.summary: Frame padding, highlighted TODOs and numbers, and a flash on each edit.
ui-polish.example: =TODO= stands out in code, and pasted text flashes briefly.

focus-mode.summary: A centred, distraction-free view for writing.
focus-mode.example: =SPC t w= centres the buffer and hides the mode line.

frames.summary: Opens each new editing surface as an OS window, for tiling window managers.
frames.example: =SPC w n= makes a window, and =SPC t f= turns the policy off for a session.

home-page.summary: A start page with recent files and projects.

popups.summary: Keeps Help and compilation output in a window that one key dismisses.

color-names.summary: Paints colour names and codes in their own colour.
color-names.example: =SPC t r= shows =#ff0000= on a red background.

help-extras.summary: Richer help pages, with source, usage examples and coloured manuals.
help-extras.example: =C-h f= shows a function's source and its callers.

command-menus.summary: Menus that list the commands of the built-in tools.
command-menus.example: =SPC c m= opens a menu of editing commands.

key-display.summary: Shows each key and its command as you press it.
key-display.example: =SPC t k= shows keys in the header line, which helps when teaching.

version-control.summary: Magit, a complete interface to Git.
version-control.example: =SPC v s= shows the status; =s= stages and =c c= commits.

diff-hl.summary: Marks changed lines in the fringe each time you save.
diff-hl.example: =SPC t g= turns the marks on or off in this buffer.

project-environment.summary: Gives each buffer its project's direnv environment.
project-environment.example: =SPC p E r= reloads it after you edit a flake.

shell-path.summary: Copies your shell's PATH, so an app launched from a menu finds your tools.
shell-path.example: An Emacs from the Dock runs the same =git= as your terminal.

terminal.summary: A fast, real terminal inside Emacs.
terminal.example: =SPC o e= opens one that full-screen programs such as =htop= run in.

eshell-highlight.summary: Colours the Eshell command line as you type.
eshell-highlight.example: =SPC o s= opens Eshell, where a misspelled command shows in red.

org-extras.summary: A tidier Org display, grouped agendas and searches across your notes.
org-extras.example: =SPC s q= finds headings by tag or state in every Org file.

linked-notes.summary: Linked notes with backlinks, for personal and project graphs.
linked-notes.example: =SPC n f= finds or creates a note.

pdf-reading.summary: Reads PDFs in Emacs and keeps notes beside each page.
pdf-reading.example: Opening a PDF renders it in a buffer, where you can search and annotate.

more-checkers.summary: Adds Flymake checkers for common tools such as linters.
more-checkers.example: =SPC F d= lists what those tools found in this buffer.

notebooks.summary: Works on Jupytext scripts as cells, with rendered maths.
notebooks.example: A =# %%= line starts a cell that you can run and step through.

jupyter.summary: Runs notebook cells in a live Jupyter kernel; it needs a native module.
jupyter.example: Set =kittymacs-notebooks-jupyter= to run a cell and see its output inline.

lang-nix.summary: Editing modes for the Nix language.
lang-nix.example: Opening a =.nix= file gives highlighting and indentation.

lang-racket.summary: Editing and a REPL for Racket.
lang-racket.example: Opening a =.rkt= file offers a REPL beside it.

lang-guile.summary: Editing and a REPL for Guile Scheme.
lang-guile.example: Opening a =.scm= file offers a Guile REPL beside it.

agents.summary: Runs a coding agent such as Claude Code in a buffer.
agents.example: =SPC a a= starts an agent in this project.

suggestions.summary: Copilot's ghost text, offered as you type once you turn it on.
suggestions.example: =SPC t a= turns suggestions on, and needs a GitHub account.

window-manager.summary: Makes Emacs the X window manager, with programs as buffers.
window-manager.example: A session that sets =KITTYMACS_EXWM=1= shows Chrome as a buffer.
